title: Keep full Dashboard frontend runs connected to their browser

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — keep full frontend runs connected (slice 4 and slice 6 CI repair)

Story and revision: .planning/seeds/SEED-413-renovate-dashboard-unit-tests.md#keep-full-frontend-runs-connected; plan .planning/slice-plans/895-keep-full-frontend-runs-connected/PLAN.md; revision f986a7ed9ae97f1dc9374d1c53d5871ce18a4681 (branch claude/keep-full-dashboard-frontend-runs-connected-to-t).

Promise: after reading the deep spec on Changes (Changes only on, out collapsed, Purpose scrolled), going to Development and back shows the same reading place without reading the story file again. Risk under review: the added wait on `.story-review-code` aria-busy="false" (story.diffContextReading) before clearing mounted.reads could hide a re-read.

Verdict (fault 1): Caught.
- Fault: dashboard/src/StoryReviewFileDiff.tsx, removed `fixed: textFixed,` from the `useReviewRead("fileText", ...)` controls, so the file's text is no longer retained per page and is read again on remount.
- Maintained check: dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-reading-place.spec.ts:141, the final assertion `expect(mounted.reads).toEqual([])` (line 167 at this revision; the caller's "line 166" is the preceding readingOffset poll).
- Observation: the test failed only at that assertion; every reading-place assertion before it still passed (Changes only checked, file pressed, diff name/code, folder toggles, scroll offset). The fixture's recorded reads showed the independent wrong behavior on the intended path: received ["story text dashboard/tests/boundary/deep/long.spec.ts"], meaning the story text was read again after returning from Development. The other test in the file still passed.
- What this shows about the risk: the aria-busy wait runs before `mounted.reads.length = 0`, so the first context read has finished before the record is cleared, and a re-read on return is still recorded and caught. The wait does not weaken the no-re-read proof on this path.

Verdict (optional fault 2): Caught.
- Fault: dashboard/src/CiProofFigures.tsx, `return changes ? [changeHeader, ...comparison] : comparison;` changed to `return comparison;`, so the Summary comparison never adds its Change column.
- Maintained check: dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-summary-story-comparison-column-sort.spec.ts. All 3 tests failed. "Summary Change keeps unchanged children last in both directions" failed in shownSortButton (`expect.element(button).toBeVisible()`) with VitestBrowserElementError "Cannot find element ... columnheader 'Change' ... button 'Change'". Its ARIA tree showed the comparison table with no Change column. The other two tests failed in 1.4 s and 1.6 s.
- Timing caveat: the Change test failed at 15341 ms, which is the default browser-test budget (dashboard/frontend.vitest.config.mts sets no timeout). It reported a locator failure that names the missing Change column, not a bare hang, but the time it took sits at the default-timeout boundary rather than well under it.

Run observations:
- Scratch: detached git worktree at the revision under /tmp; npm ci with Node 24.21.0. The pre-probe state was clean. Focused command: `env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES npx vitest run --config dashboard/frontend.vitest.config.mts --maxWorkers=1 <spec>`.
- Baseline: both specs passed, 2 files and 5 tests, 2.10 s.
- Reach: in fault run 1 the named test reached line 167 (its trace lists every earlier step passing). In fault run 2 the Change header lookup ran against a rendered comparison table.
- Restoration: each edit was reverted with git checkout through a shell trap. Afterwards git diff was empty and only untracked .vitest/ run artifacts remained. Rerunning both specs gave 2 files and 5 tests passing in 1.66 s. The scratch worktree was then removed, and the reviewed checkout is unchanged (clean status).

Next proof action: none needed for fault 1. For fault 2, optionally make the missing-Change-column failure arrive sooner than the default budget, for example with a shorter wait in shownSortButton once the comparison table is shown. That is the caller's call. This matches the slice 6 CI-repair intent (wait for comparison columns before sorting); it is a recognition, not a new repair decision.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Vitest "Duration"): baseline 2.10 s; fault 1 1.44 s; fault 2 about 18.3 s file time (19.7 s wall, measured with node Date.now); restored 1.66 s. Total about 23.5 s of runner time.
- Human effort: unavailable; no human interaction during this probe.
- Agent effort: unavailable as a measured figure; no token counter is exposed to this subagent. Estimated about 20 tool calls.

- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 107103 ms (measured), from 1795857534587 to 1795857641690 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

Wrap-up disposition: f986a7ed9ae97f1dc9374d1c53d5871ce18a4681, Caught (both faults); no follow-up. The fault 2 failure names the missing column within the default budget, so no stronger proof is needed.
